summary: A 1924 pole-platform lookout in Glacier National Park replaced in 1933 by the current two-story timber structure, NRHP-listed in 1986 and reportedly still staffed by the Park Service in summer.

facts.design: Two-story timber-frame lookout with pyramidal roof, built to a modified U.S. Forest Service plan; replaced a 1924 10-ft pole platform with log cabin

staffing.as_of: unknown (per firelookout.com summary, not independently dated)

access.note: Located within Glacier National Park; access and any climbing would be governed by NPS, not open for casual public climbing

events.note: First lookout: a 10-ft pole platform with log cabin living quarters
NPS replaced the 1924 structure with the current two-story timber lookout
Added to NRHP February 14, 1986 as part of the Glacier National Park Multiple Property Submission, reference 86000346
Registered with National Historic Lookout Register September 15, 1991

evidence.supports: low two-story timber structure with pyramidal roof, built 1933, replacing a 1923/1924 structure, per modified USFS plan
evidence.quote: The low two-story timber-construction structure with a pyramidal roof was built in 1933, replacing a similar structure built in 1923. It is one of several similar structures built to a modified version of a plan developed by the U.S. Forest Service.

evidence.supports: significant as one of a chain of staffed fire lookout posts within Glacier
evidence.quote: The Huckleberry Fire Lookout in Glacier National Park is significant as one of a chain of staffed fire lookout posts within the park.

evidence.supports: NRHP reference number 86000346, built year 1933 per NRHP infobox
evidence.quote:
Built 1933
MPS Glacier National Park MRA

evidence.supports: first developed 1924 with 10-ft pole platform and log cabin, replaced 1933 with present 2-story NPS frame cabin; staffed in summer
evidence.quote: Huckleberry was first developed in 1924 with a 10' pole platform and log cabin living quarters, replaced in 1933 with the present 2-story NPS frame cabin. It is staffed in the summer.

corrections.proposed: 1933 (current structure), with an earlier 1924 pole-platform predecessor noted separately
corrections.why: The brief's single 'built: 1924' field conflates two different structures. Wikipedia and firelookout.com both describe a first lookout from the mid-1920s (Wikipedia says 1923, firelookout.com says 1924) that was replaced in 1933 by the two-story timber lookout that stands today. The 1933 date is the one that matches the NRHP listing and the currently standing structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia (citing the NRHP nomination) says the 1933 lookout replaced a structure built in 1923; firelookout.com says the first development was in 1924. Both agree the current two-story structure dates to 1933; the one-year discrepancy on the predecessor's date is left unresolved and noted here.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 'built: 1924' field is likely referring to the original pole-platform predecessor, not the structure now standing (built 1933); flagged as a correction. The current staffing claim comes only from firelookout.com, a hobbyist site with no visible date on that claim, so it is not strongly corroborated -- an NPS source confirming present-day staffing would strengthen this. Did not attempt to retrieve the NRHP nomination PDF itself (npgallery asset page returned only a metadata summary, not the full nomination text) or the NHLR newspaper-article PDF due to the per-tower read budget. Editorial pass 2026-10-04 fixed two footnote misattributions in the story: the 1924 pole-platform/log-cabin sentence was cited to Wikipedia ([^2]) but that detail is only in firelookout.com ([^3]); the 'chain of staffed fire lookouts' sentence was cited to NHLR ([^1]) but the quote is on Wikipedia ([^2]). The NRHP+NHLR registration sentence was missing a [^2] cite for the NRHP facts.
